nodes.name: 0000_same_silver_surfer.sql
nodes.summary: Initial Drizzle migration that creates the baseline local SQLite schema for accounts, categories, incomes, expenses, expense scheduler, sync meta, mutation queue, conflicts, and app settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Drizzle's '--> statement-breakpoint' marker between statements so the migrator can run them in separate statements under a single transaction.

nodes.name: accounts
nodes.summary: Mirror of the Notion Accounts database: stores account identity, type, starting balance, credit metadata, and Notion edit tracking.

nodes.name: app_settings
nodes.summary: Generic key/value table for app-level settings and small persistent flags.

nodes.name: conflicts
nodes.summary: Records three-way merge conflicts (base/local/remote per field) detected during sync, with resolution metadata.

nodes.name: expense_categories
nodes.summary: Mirror of Notion expense categories, including monthly budget and auxiliary flag used for workflows.

nodes.name: expense_scheduler
nodes.summary: Recurring expense templates that generate expense rows on schedule, with frequency, next-run date, and active flag.

nodes.name: expenses
nodes.summary: Mirror of the Notion Expenses database with payment tracking, pasabuy fields, credit-card linkage, and soft-delete support.

nodes.name: income_categories
nodes.summary: Mirror of Notion income categories with source label and auxiliary flag.

nodes.name: incomes
nodes.summary: Mirror of the Notion Incomes database with gross/capital split, transaction-account linkage, and credit-card payment coverage.

nodes.name: mutation_queue
nodes.summary: Outbox queue of pending local mutations awaiting push to Notion, with attempts and last-error tracking.

nodes.name: sync_meta
nodes.summary: Generic key/value table used by the sync layer to track cursors, last-run timestamps, and configuration flags.

nodes.name: 0001_kind_nekra.sql
nodes.summary: Adds pasabuy payment date and paid-period columns to the expenses table to support pasabuy installment tracking.

nodes.name: 0002_add_account_qr_code.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a qr_code text column to the accounts table to store an optional account QR code reference.

nodes.name: 0003_reflective_angel.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the activity_log table that records sync actions and lifecycle events for the History page.

nodes.name: activity_log
nodes.summary: Per-record activity log capturing resource, action, direction, title, and Notion page id for sync events.

nodes.name: 0004_massive_maximus.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a run_id column to activity_log so log entries can be grouped under a single sync run identifier.

nodes.name: 0005_chat.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the chat agent tables: chat_credentials, chat_threads, and chat_messages, with supporting indexes for thread and message lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: API keys are intentionally NOT stored here; only a key_fingerprint is persisted while secrets live in the OS safeStorage vault.

nodes.name: chat_credentials
nodes.summary: Stores chat provider credential metadata (name, key fingerprint, default flag) while secrets remain in safeStorage.

nodes.name: chat_threads
nodes.summary: Stores chat conversation threads with title, credential, model, and overlay selection plus timestamps.

nodes.name: chat_messages
nodes.summary: Append-only message log for chat threads, with role, content, optional structured payload JSON, and created timestamp.

nodes.name: 0006_chat_drafts.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the chat_drafts table for durable, confirm-gated proposals that survive app restarts until the user Approves or Cancels.

nodes.name: chat_drafts
nodes.summary: Durable store of chat-proposed creates/updates with status, missing required fields, warnings, payload, target ids, and a computed preview.

nodes.name: 0007_chat_draft_display.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a presentation-only display column to chat_drafts so the confirm card can show resolved names and amounts instead of raw ids.

nodes.name: 0008_reference_icons.sql
nodes.summary: Adds an icon column to accounts, income_categories, and expense_categories to cache Notion page icons locally (data URIs or emoji).

nodes.name: 0009_activity_payload.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a payload column to activity_log so the History page can render full read-only form modals for synced income and expense items.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand what Notable Finance is: an offline-first Electron desktop app where local SQLite is the source of truth and Notion is a bidirectional mirror. The README explains the architecture, phase completion status (Phases 0-5), and development setup so you get the big picture before diving into code.

tour.title: Electron Entry & Window Management
tour.description: The Electron main process entry point bootstraps the app, initializes the database, registers IPC handlers, creates the main window, and starts the auto-updater. The window manager handles window creation, menu installation with keyboard shortcuts, and macOS activate handling. These two files together are where the app comes to life.
tour.languageLesson: Electron apps have a main process (Node.js) that creates BrowserWindow instances. The renderer process runs the UI. Communication between them uses IPC via contextBridge for security.

tour.title: Project Configuration & Build Pipeline
tour.description: package.json defines the entire dependency tree (React 19, better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, electron-updater) and npm scripts for dev/build/test. electron-builder.yml configures packaging for macOS, Linux, and Windows with auto-update support. electron-vite orchestrates the build for main, preload, and renderer processes.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The baseline Drizzle migration defines the full local SQLite schema: accounts, income/expense categories, incomes, expenses, expense scheduler, mutation queue (outbox), conflicts (three-way merge), sync_meta, and app_settings. Later migrations add pasabuy tracking, activity log, chat tables, draft display, reference icons, and activity payloads. This schema is the backbone of the offline-first architecture.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle migrations use '-- statement-breakpoint' markers so the migrator runs each statement separately under a single transaction. Migrations are idempotent and ordered sequentially.

tour.title: Data Access Layer
tour.description: The database index initializes the SQLite connection and runs pending migrations on startup. The Drizzle schema file defines typed table objects that mirror the SQL schema. Repositories contain all CRUD operations for incomes, expenses, accounts, categories, and scheduler records with soft-delete support. Mappers translate database rows into typed domain objects.

tour.title: Domain Logic & Validation
tour.description: Domain derivations compute account balances, category spending, dashboard summaries, and monthly monitoring reports by composing raw data. Validation enforces ISO dates, finite numbers, and required fields on create/update inputs. Notion formulas replicate the hidden Notion formula logic (transaction amounts, installment math, pasabuy splits) so the app remains consistent with Notion.

tour.title: Notion Integration
tour.description: The Notion service layer manages client initialization, database discovery, and schema verification against the expected Notion database definitions. The HTTP client handles all Notion API calls with error classification. Page extractors parse Notion API responses into typed field values. The property mapper converts app DTOs back into Notion page properties for writes.

tour.title: Bidirectional Sync Engine
tour.description: The sync engine is the heart of the offline-first design. Pull fetches the latest Notion data and reconciles it locally via a three-way merge algorithm that detects per-field differences between base, local, and remote versions. Push sends local mutations (from the outbox queue) to Notion with retry/backoff. Conflicts are stored for user resolution. The scheduler runs periodic sync.
tour.languageLesson: Three-way merge compares base (last-synced state), local (current SQLite), and remote (current Notion). When local and remote diverge from the same base, a conflict is recorded per field, and the user must choose which version to keep.

tour.title: IPC Handlers & Preload Bridge
tour.description: IPC handlers register all invoke-based channels that the renderer calls for finance operations, settings, sync, chat, and dev logs. The preload script exposes a structured, typed API to the renderer via contextBridge, wrapping every invoke call. This is the security boundary: the renderer never accesses Node.js APIs directly.
tour.languageLesson: contextBridge creates a safe, isolated bridge between the renderer and main process. The renderer gets a window.api object with typed methods instead of raw ipcRenderer access, following Electron security best practices.

tour.title: Renderer Entry & Workspace
tour.description: The HTML entry point mounts the React app. The main.tsx renders the root component inside providers for theme, finance data, UI settings, app tabs, and keyboard shortcuts. FinanceWorkspace orchestrates the entire UI: it manages layout, sync state, navigation between pages, and data hydration on startup.

tour.title: Finance Pages & UI Components
tour.description: Each finance section has a dedicated page component: Dashboard shows summary metrics and charts, Income and Expense provide data tables with create/edit/delete forms, Monitoring displays budget status, Accounts shows gallery/table views, and History renders activity log entries with detail modals. The UI layer uses shared form modals, data tables, search bars, and charts.

tour.title: AI Chat Subsystem
tour.description: The chat subsystem provides an AI assistant for natural-language finance queries and operations. The orchestrator routes user intent through skill detection, tool execution loops, and provider calls. Read tools query the database (dashboard summary, incomes, expenses, budgets), while write tools propose creates/updates through a draft-and-confirm workflow. API keys are stored encrypted via Electron safeStorage.

tour.title: Testing & Packaging
tour.description: The project uses Vitest for unit tests (domain logic, sync, chat, mappers) and Playwright for Electron end-to-end tests (window loading, keyboard shortcuts). The test suite covers validation, derivations, merge logic, Notion integration, and chat hardening. electron-builder packages the app for distribution with auto-update support via GitHub Releases.
